title: Hypothesis-driven promptset litmus and adaptive AB failure-mode plan for Optimize
creator: Rina Patel
description:
Background:
Optimize requires a lightweight, repeatable evaluation framework that detects regressions on production-shaped prompt cohorts and provides deterministic A/B decisioning rules. Current PRDs focus on broad sampling and multi-metric thresholds; this ticket defines a hypothesis-driven litmus process for promptsets plus an adaptive failure-mode plan for AB experiments with automated rollback triggers.

Goals:
- Define a compact "litmus" promptset sampling process (<=200 prompts) that surfaces likely regressions for a given model change without running full-scale evals.
- Specify multi-metric thresholds (primary quality, safety, latency) and a decision lattice for AB stop/rollback actions.
- Design an adaptive failure-mode where the system widens or tightens thresholds depending on cohort volatility and customer exposure.
- Produce acceptance criteria and rollout gating that Product, Research, and SRE can rely on for safe canaries.

Scope (in):
- Litmus promptset generation rules (stratified by customer cohorts, usage Z-order, and failure modes).
- A/B stop rules: high-confidence statistical tests, effect size bounds, and aggregated signal scoring.
- Automated guardrail actions (traffic diversion to prior model, scale-back of new variant, notify-once vs notify-on-every-incident).
- Implementation-ready metadata and observability hooks (metric names, dashboards referenced).

Scope (out):
- Full-scale long-tail fuzz testing and continuous drift detection infrastructure (handled by separate Optimize eval infra tickets).
- Per-customer contractual rollback workflows for Dedicated/Private customers (enterprise playbook handled by PM-XXXX).

Non-functional constraints:
- Litmus run must complete in < 10 minutes for typical Optimize runs (to be feasible during canaries).
- AB stop evaluation must not require >30 minutes of aggregated traffic to reach a decision for high-frequency endpoints.

Success metrics:
- False-negative regression rate < 10% vs existing full eval baseline on held-out releases.
- Average time-to-decision for canaries <= 20 minutes for 95% of experiments.

Deliverables:
- Short PRD (this doc + acceptance criteria) and a test harness specification for ENG.
- A canonical litmus promptset generator algorithm and sample output for three production cohorts.
- A decision lattice YAML that maps metric signals to actions (abort, degrade, monitor, proceed).
- Reference dashboards and a runbook snippet for SRE/PM on-canary triage.
Acceptance_criteria: Litmus sampling algorithm documented with reproducible steps and a sample 200-prompt file for each of three cohorts (consumer-chat, docs-summarization, search-rewrite)

Primary quality metric: cohort-level ROUGE-like nDCG or custom scoring per cohort with clear calculation and 95% CI; regression threshold defined (absolute and relative) and validated on two prior releases
Safety sentinel: at-least-one high-severity safety check (eg. toxic content rate) flagged with absolute maximum tolerated rate; exceed -> immediate abort
Latency sentinel: median token latency increase > 25% triggers a degraded-traffic action (route 50% to control), tail > 95th percentile latency increase > 40% -> abort
AB decision rules encoded as deterministic steps: preflight checks -> litmus pass -> canary(5% traffic, 30m) -> analyze signals -> action chosen from lattice
Automated rollback actions implemented as clear outcomes: abort to previous pinned model, degrade traffic to X%, or escalate to oncall; each action has a required notification/annotation

Adaptive threshold mechanism specified: how threshold widens/narrows based on cohort volatility (statistical variance) and customer exposure, with simulation on historical data showing expected tradeoffs
Runbook: triage checklist, who to call, required dashboards, and example GitHub PR and Confluence links included
Performance constraints met: end-to-end litmus run time < 10m in reference environment, and canary decision logic computes within 30m for medium traffic endpoints
notes: Tradeoffs: smaller litmus sets reduce compute and speed decisions but increase false negatives; we recommend starting with 150-200 prompts and iterating based on observed FN rate.
Edge case: New model architectures with shifted tokenization may require a short normalization step before litmus scoring; flagging for ENG to handle tokenization mapping.
Rollout strategy: Start as advisory-only for first 3 releases, then switch to automated abort for high-severity safety signals only.
Metrics and dashboard names: optimize.litmus.primary_score, optimize.litmus.safety_rate, optimize.litmus.latency_median, optimize.ab.decision_time
Fallbacks: If litmus results are inconclusive after the time window, default to conservative action (degrade traffic) and trigger human-in-the-loop review.
Parallel work: ENG to expose new metric tags and a canary traffic knob before release (dependency ENG-21761).
